name: Turtle and Three Sequences
description: Piggy gives Turtle three sequences $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$, $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$, and $$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$. Turtle will choose a subsequence of $$$1, 2, \ldots, n$$$ of length $$$m$$$, let it be $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_m$$$. The subsequence should satisfy the following conditions: $$$a_{p_1} \le a_{p_2} \le \cdots \le a_{p_m}$$$; All $$$b_{p_i}$$$ for all indices $$$i$$$ are pairwise distinct , i.e., there don't exist two different indices $$$i$$$, $$$j$$$ such that $$$b_{p_i} = b_{p_j}$$$. Help him find the maximum value of $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^m c_{p_i}$$$, or tell him that it is impossible to choose a subsequence of length $$$m$$$ that satisfies the conditions above. Recall that a sequence $$$a$$$ is a subsequence of a sequence $$$b$$$ if $$$a$$$ can be obtained from $$$b$$$ by the deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3000$$$, $$$1 \le m \le 5$$$) — the lengths of the three sequences and the required length of the subsequence. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the elements of the sequence $$$a$$$. The third line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le n$$$) — the elements of the sequence $$$b$$$. The fourth line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n$$$ ($$$1 \le c_i \le 10^4$$$) — the elements of the sequence $$$c$$$.
output_specification: Output a single integer — the maximum value of $$$\sum\limits_{i = 1}^m c_{p_i}$$$. If it is impossible to choose a subsequence of length $$$m$$$ that satisfies the conditions above, output $$$-1$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2003F — Turtle and Three Sequences [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
